entities.summary:
The President of the Philippines is the head of state and head of government of the Philippines. This office has been held by various individuals since the country's independence from Spain in 1898. The President serves as both the chief executive and the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, with powers to appoint and dismiss cabinet members and military officers.

The President is elected by the people through a presidential election held every six years, with no term limits. The election process involves a complex system of electors who cast their votes for the president and vice president.

The President's role is crucial in shaping the country's foreign policy, economy, and social welfare programs. They also have the power to declare martial law and suspend the writ of habeas corpus in times of emergency.

One notable instance of the President's impact on the country is the legacy of President Ferdinand Marcos, who ruled the Philippines from 1965 to 1986. His regime was marked by widespread corruption, human rights abuses, and economic stagnation. The People Power Revolution of 1986, led by Corazon Aquino, eventually toppled Marcos' government and restored democracy to the country.

As Cory Aquino once said, 'We must not forget the lessons of history, lest we repeat the mistakes of the past.'
